D.t: John Hickenlooper leads by 22.3 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 630,658 votes; a one point swing is about 14,159 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +13.5 and D +30.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +22.4. Your best recent poll is Research Co. at D +24.0; your worst is Lake Research Partners (D) at D +10.9. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 223,574 votes; Boulder, a projected net 112,815 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 104,475 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, D +0.1, 11.9% of the vote; Douglas, D +1.2, 7.1% of the vote; Montezuma, R +10.5, 0.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, John Hickenlooper runs furthest behind in Weld, Larimer, Boulder. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 57 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.08 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 60 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Voters without a degree, 48% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.41 points.
The forecast's worst groups for John Hickenlooper: Immigration voters 32 to 66, Small counties 49 to 49, Midsize counties 52 to 46. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.1M cash against $28K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
